THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:21587  MFA No. 421 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 7828 of 2018  JUDGMENT

The appeals by the claimant and the Insurance Company are filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, challenging the judgment and award dated 21.08.2017 passed in MVC No. 891/2001 by the learned Principal Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hassan.
2.

The claimant sustained injuries in a road traffic accident on 18.08.2012 when the rider of the offending motorcycle, who was riding rashly and negligently, collided with the claimant while he was proceeding as a pillion rider on the motorcycle.
Consequently, the claimant filed a petition seeking just and proper compensation.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,53,344/- with interest at 6% per annum.
The claimant is appealing for an enhancement of the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal, while the Insurance Company is appealing against the quantum of compensation.

3. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
4.
The claimant sustained injuries in the road traffic accident on 18.08.2012 and was 23 years old at the time of the accident.

In the absence of proof of income, the claimant's notional income is assessed at Rs.7,000/- per month, as opposed to the Rs.9,000/- per month assessed by the Tribunal, which included an addition of 50% towards loss of future prospects.

The doctor, who was examined as PW2, testified that the claimant sustained unhealed sockets,
distorted occlusion, facial asymmetry, difficulty in chewing, and difficulty in speech due to the accident, resulting in a physical disability of 25%.

In his cross- examination, PW2 stated that although the claimant has no difficulty in continuing his work as an attender, the claimant does experience difficulty in chewing and speaking, which would certainly hinder his ability to perform his duties effectively.
6.
Although the permanent disability was assessed at 7%, the Tribunal erroneously added 50% of the income towards loss of future prospects, which is impermissible..

Therefore, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:

due to disability 7000 x 12 x 18 x 7%
Pain and suffering 30,000/- 12,000/-
Medical Expenses 55,264/- 55,264/-
Loss of amenities 30,000/- 30,000/-
Food and nourishment 20,000/- 20,000/-
charges Total 2,41,104/- 2,53,344/-
7.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards medical expenses, loss of amenities and food and nourishment charges remains unaltered.

The claimant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,41,104/- as against Rs.2,53,344/- awarded by the Tribunal, and shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till actual realization
The compensation awarded by the tribunal is reduced by Rs.12,240/-.
To this extent, the impugned award stands modified.
9. The Statutory amount in deposit by the respondent - Insurance Company to be transmitted the jurisdictional Tribunal.
10. MFA No.421/2018 is allowed in part, and MFA No.7828/2018 is dismissed.
